Match the group (when cited as a substituent prefix) in List-I with its prefix in List-II.

List-I:
A. –OH
B. –NO₂
C. –OCH₃
D. >C=O (ketonic, as a substituent)

List-II:
I. Oxo
II. Methoxy
III. Hydroxy
IV. Nitro

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Prefixes for substituent groups in IUPAC names
solution.explanation: When these groups are not the principal group (or, for –NO₂ and –OR, always), they are cited as prefixes: hydroxy, nitro, methoxy (alkoxy) and oxo.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', IUPAC nomenclature (functional groups)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Carbocations behave as electrophiles.
Reason (R): The positively charged carbon of a carbocation has only six electrons in its valence shell.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: With only a sextet of electrons, the carbocation carbon is electron deficient and seeks an electron pair, which is what makes it an electrophile.
steps: A: carbocations accept electron pairs → electrophiles → true
Electron deficiency is the reason it seeks electrons → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', carbocations
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: A compound contains –OH, –NH₂, a C=C bond and a –CHO group. In its IUPAC name, which group is the principal functional group (cited as the suffix)?

solution.concept: Order of preference of functional groups
solution.explanation: NCERT's order of preference: –COOH > –SO₃H > –COOR > –COCl > –CONH₂ > –CN > –CHO > >C=O > –OH > –NH₂ > C=C > C≡C. Of the four groups here, –CHO ranks highest.
steps: Compare positions in the preference order
So the suffix is -al; –OH and –NH₂ become prefixes (hydroxy, amino)
solution.why_others_wrong: –OH, –NH₂ and C=C all rank below –CHO, so they cannot supply the suffix here.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature of polyfunctional compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following groups, attached to a benzene ring, show an electron-withdrawing resonance (−R) effect?
–NO₂, –CN, –CHO, –COOH, –OH, –NH₂, –OCH₃, –Cl

solution.explanation: Groups with a π bond to a more electronegative atom conjugated with the ring (–NO₂, –CN, –CHO, –COOH) pull π electrons out of the ring (−R). Groups with a lone pair on the atom attached to the ring (–OH, –NH₂, –OCH₃, –Cl) donate electrons by resonance (+R).
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 leaves out one of the −R groups. 5 or 6 count –Cl (and –OCH₃), whose −I effect is electron-withdrawing but whose resonance effect is +R.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', resonance effect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(Cl)–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH₃ is:

solution.explanation: Both directions of numbering give the locant set {2, 4}. When the sets tie, the substituent cited first in alphabetical order (chloro before methyl) gets the lower number.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4-Chloro-2-methylpentane gives the lower number to methyl, against the alphabetical rule. 2-Methyl-4-chloropentane does not cite the prefixes alphabetically. 1-Chloro-1,3-dimethylbutane does not use the longest chain.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', IUPAC nomenclature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Methyl ethanoate and ethyl methanoate are functional group isomers.
Statement II: Butanal and butan-2-one are chain isomers.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Methyl ethanoate (CH₃COOCH₃) and ethyl methanoate (HCOOC₂H₅) are both esters; they differ only in the alkyl groups on either side of the functional group, so they are metamers. Butanal (aldehyde) and butan-2-one (ketone) have different functional groups, so they are functional group isomers, not chain isomers.
steps: Statement I: same functional group (ester) → metamers, not functional isomers → false
Statement II: aldehyde vs ketone → functional group isomers → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', structural isomerism
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Both carbon–oxygen bonds in the ethanoate ion, CH₃COO⁻, have the same length.
Reason (R): In ethanoic acid itself, the two carbon–oxygen bonds also have the same length.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The ethanoate ion is a resonance hybrid of two equivalent structures, so both C–O bonds are identical. In ethanoic acid, one bond is C=O and the other C–OH; the two equivalent structures are not possible, so the bonds differ in length.
steps: A: equivalent canonical forms → equal C–O bonds → true
R: acid has one C=O and one C–OH → unequal → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', resonance structure
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the reaction in List-I with the reactive species that attacks or is formed in its key step (List-II).

List-I:
A. CH₄ + Cl₂ in diffused sunlight
B. Hydrolysis of (CH₃)₃C–Br in water (SN1)
C. Nitration of benzene with a mixture of conc. HNO₃ and conc. H₂SO₄
D. Addition of HCN to CH₃CHO in the presence of a little base

List-II:
I. Cyanide ion attacking the carbonyl carbon
II. Nitronium ion, NO₂⁺
III. Chlorine free radical, Cl•
IV. tert-Butyl carbocation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Light causes homolysis of Cl₂, so chlorination of methane is a free radical chain. SN1 hydrolysis of a tertiary bromide goes through the (CH₃)₃C⁺ ion. Nitration uses the nitronium ion as the electrophile. In cyanohydrin formation, CN⁻ (made from HCN by the base) attacks the carbonyl carbon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', reaction mechanism
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following IUPAC names are correct?

(a) CH₃–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–OH: 2-methylbutan-1-ol
(b) CH₃–CH=CH–CH₂–OH: but-2-en-1-ol
(c) CH₃–CH(NH₂)–CH₃: propan-2-amine
(d) CH₂=CH–CHO: prop-1-enal
(e) Cl–CH₂–COOH: 1-chloroethanoic acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The carbon of –CHO or –COOH is C-1. So CH₂=CH–CHO is prop-2-enal (double bond between C-2 and C-3), and ClCH₂COOH is chloroethanoic (2-chloroethanoic) acid, since C-1 is the carboxyl carbon. The other three names follow the rules: the –OH or –NH₂ carbon gets the lowest number.
steps: (a) OH on C-1, CH₃ on C-2 → true
(b) OH on C-1, C=C from C-2 → true
(e) C-1 is COOH; Cl is on C-2 → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (d) or (e), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', IUPAC nomenclature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Ignoring hyperconjugation, how many of the following show resonance (delocalisation of π electrons or of a lone pair through a π system)?
Aniline, ethanamine, chloroethene (CH₂=CHCl), phenol, ethanol, propene, chloroethane

solution.explanation: Resonance needs a lone pair or π bond conjugated with another π system. In aniline and phenol the N or O lone pair is conjugated with the ring; in chloroethene a Cl lone pair is conjugated with the C=C bond.
steps: Aniline, phenol: lone pair + ring → resonance
Chloroethene: Cl lone pair + C=C → resonance
Ethanamine, ethanol, chloroethane: no π system
Propene: only one C=C, no conjugated lone pair (hyperconjugation only)
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 misses chloroethene. 4 or 5 count propene (whose only delocalisation is hyperconjugation, excluded here) or a saturated compound with no π system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', resonance effect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
In how many of the following carbocations is the positive charge delocalised through conjugation with a C=C bond or a benzene ring (not counting hyperconjugation)?
CH₂=CH–CH₂⁺, C₆H₅–CH₂⁺, (CH₃)₃C⁺, CH₃–CH₂⁺, CH₂=CH–CH⁺–CH₃, C₆H₅–CH⁺–CH₃, (CH₃)₂CH⁺

solution.concept: Resonance stabilisation of allylic and benzylic carbocations
solution.explanation: Delocalisation through a π system needs the positive carbon to be directly attached to a C=C or a benzene ring (allylic or benzylic). Alkyl cations are stabilised only by +I and hyperconjugation.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 or 3 leave out the substituted allylic or benzylic ions. 5 counts the tert-butyl cation, which is very stable but only through +I and hyperconjugation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', carbocations; resonance

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The tert-butyl cation, (CH₃)₃C⁺, is less stable than the methyl cation, CH₃⁺.
Reason (R): Alkyl groups attached to the positively charged carbon release electrons to it (inductive effect and hyperconjugation) and disperse the positive charge.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Electron release by the three methyl groups (+I and hyperconjugation) disperses the charge of (CH₃)₃C⁺, so the order of stability is (CH₃)₃C⁺ > (CH₃)₂CH⁺ > CH₃CH₂⁺ > CH₃⁺. The assertion reverses this.
steps: A: tertiary cation is the most stable → A false
R: correct description of alkyl group effects → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', carbocations
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Among the canonical structures of a molecule, those with greater separation of opposite charges contribute more to the resonance hybrid.
Statement II: The greater the number of important contributing structures, the greater the resonance energy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Rules for the relative importance of canonical structures
solution.explanation: Structures with more covalent bonds, every atom (except H) with an octet, less separation of opposite charges and negative charge on the more electronegative atom contribute more. NCERT also notes that more important contributing structures mean a larger resonance energy.
steps: Statement I: less (not more) charge separation means a larger contribution → false
Statement II: true as NCERT states
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', resonance structure
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match each pair of compounds in List-I with the relationship between them in List-II.

List-I:
A. cis-But-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene
B. The two non-superimposable mirror-image forms of butan-2-ol
C. Propan-1-ol and methoxyethane
D. Hexan-2-one and hexan-3-one

List-II:
I. Position isomers
II. Functional group isomers
III. Optical isomers (enantiomers)
IV. Geometrical isomers

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: cis/trans forms differ in the arrangement about a double bond (geometrical); mirror-image forms of a chiral molecule are enantiomers (optical); an alcohol and an ether of the same formula differ in functional group; the two hexanones differ only in the position of the carbonyl group.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', isomerism
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are correct rules of IUPAC nomenclature?

(a) The parent chain is the longest chain that contains the principal functional group.
(b) The chain is numbered so that the substituents get the lowest set of locants, compared at the first point of difference.
(c) The chain is numbered so that the carbon bearing the principal functional group gets the lowest possible number.
(d) Multiplying prefixes such as di- and tri- are taken into account when substituent names are arranged alphabetically.
(e) In a carboxylic acid containing a C=C bond, the double bond gets locant 1 in preference to the carboxyl carbon.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The principal group decides the parent chain and gets the lowest locant (the –COOH carbon is always C-1). Lowest locants are compared at the first point of difference. Multiplying prefixes (di, tri) are ignored when alphabetising: e.g. 'ethyl' comes before 'dimethyl'.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (d) or (e), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', IUPAC nomenclature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of (CH₃)₃C–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH(CH₃)₂ is:

solution.concept: Longest chain and lowest set of locants
solution.explanation: The longest chain has six carbons: CH₃–C(CH₃)₂–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH(CH₃)–CH₃. Numbering from the tert-butyl end gives {2,2,4,5}; from the other end {2,3,5,5}. At the first point of difference (second locant) 2 < 3, so the first set is chosen.
steps: Longest chain: 6 C (hexane) with four methyl groups
solution.why_others_wrong: 2,3,5,5 numbers from the wrong end. 2,4,5,5 is not a possible set of locants for this molecule. A heptane chain cannot be traced in it; the longest chain has six carbons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', IUPAC nomenclature (branched alkanes)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following alkanes cannot be prepared by the Wurtz reaction?

solution.explanation: In the Wurtz reaction, two alkyl groups join, so the product always has at least two carbon atoms (ethane from CH₃Br, butane from C₂H₅Br, hexane from C₃H₇Br). Methane, with one carbon, cannot be made this way.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ethane, butane and hexane are R–R products of CH₃X, C₂H₅X and n-C₃H₇X respectively.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', preparation of alkanes (Wurtz reaction)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the Newman projection of the staggered conformation of ethane, the smallest dihedral angle between a C–H bond on the front carbon and a C–H bond on the rear carbon is:

solution.explanation: Seen along the C–C axis, the three C–H bonds on each carbon are 120° apart. In the staggered form the rear bonds lie exactly between the front bonds, so the smallest dihedral angle is 120°/2 = 60°. In the eclipsed form it is 0°.
steps: C–H bonds on one carbon: 360°/3 = 120° apart in projection
Staggered: rear bonds bisect the front ones → 60°
solution.why_others_wrong: 0° is the eclipsed conformation. 120° is the angle between two bonds on the same carbon. 109.5° is the tetrahedral bond angle, not a dihedral angle.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', conformations of ethane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Benzene was first isolated by Kekulé in 1865.
Statement II: The molecular formula of benzene, C₆H₆, indicates a high degree of unsaturation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: benzene was isolated by Michael Faraday in 1825. Kekulé proposed its cyclic structure with alternating single and double bonds in 1865. The formula C₆H₆ indicates a high degree of unsaturation.
steps: Statement I: Faraday isolated it (1825); Kekulé gave the structure (1865) → false
Statement II: C₆H₆ vs C₆H₁₄ for hexane → highly unsaturated → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', aromatic hydrocarbons (structure of benzene)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the class of hydrocarbon in List-I with its general formula in List-II.

List-I:
A. Open-chain alkanes
B. Open-chain alkenes (one C=C)
C. Open-chain alkynes (one C≡C)
D. Benzene and its alkyl homologues

List-II:
I. CₙH₂ₙ₋₆
II. CₙH₂ₙ₋₂
III. CₙH₂ₙ
IV. CₙH₂ₙ₊₂

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Each ring or π bond removes two hydrogen atoms from CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. An alkene (one π bond) is CₙH₂ₙ, an alkyne (two π bonds) CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, and benzene and its alkyl homologues (one ring + three π bonds) CₙH₂ₙ₋₆.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', classification and general formulas
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Alkanes release a large amount of heat on complete combustion.
Reason (R): All the carbon atoms in an alkane are sp³ hybridised.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Combustion of alkanes to CO₂ and H₂O is strongly exothermic, which is why they are used as fuels. That all the carbons are sp³ hybridised is also true but describes their bonding geometry, not why combustion releases energy.
steps: A: e.g. CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O, ΔcH° = −890 kJ mol⁻¹ → true
R: alkanes are saturated, sp³ carbons → true
Hybridisation does not explain the heat released → R is not the explanation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkanes (structure; combustion)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the chlorination of benzene with Cl₂ in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃, the role of AlCl₃ is to:

options.text: absorb the HCl formed and shift the equilibrium
act as a Lewis acid that generates the Cl⁺ electrophile

solution.concept: Generation of the electrophile in halogenation
solution.explanation: AlCl₃ accepts a chloride ion from Cl₂ (Cl₂ + AlCl₃ → Cl⁺ + [AlCl₄]⁻). The Cl⁺ electrophile attacks the ring to give the arenium ion, which loses H⁺ to form chlorobenzene.
steps: AlCl₃ is electron deficient → Lewis acid
solution.why_others_wrong: Free radicals form in light, which leads to addition (benzene hexachloride), not ring substitution. AlCl₃ neither absorbs HCl to drive the reaction nor acts as a reductant.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', electrophilic substitution reactions (mechanism)
solution.final_answer: Option C: act as a Lewis acid that generates the Cl⁺ electrophile

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Methane reacts with steam at 1273 K in the presence of nickel:
CH₄ + H₂O → CO + 3H₂
The volume of hydrogen, measured at STP, obtained from 8.0 g of methane is (C = 12, H = 1; molar volume at STP = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.concept: Stoichiometry of the reaction of methane with steam
solution.explanation: One mole of methane gives three moles of hydrogen.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11.2 L takes a 1 : 1 ratio. 44.8 L adds the CO (0.5 mol) to the hydrogen. 22.4 L takes two moles of H₂ per mole of methane.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', chemical properties of alkanes (reaction with steam)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 12.3 g of 1-bromopropane is heated with alcoholic KOH and converted completely into propene. The volume of propene at STP is (C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80; molar volume at STP = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.explanation: CH₃CH₂CH₂Br + KOH (alc) → CH₃CH=CH₂ + KBr + H₂O: one mole of alkyl halide gives one mole of alkene.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.12 L halves the moles, as if two molecules of halide gave one alkene. 4.48 L doubles them. 3.36 L multiplies by 1.5, as if three carbon atoms mattered.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', preparation of alkenes from alkyl halides

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the structure of benzene are correct?

(a) Kekulé proposed a cyclic arrangement of six carbon atoms with alternate single and double bonds.
(b) Benzene forms only one monosubstituted derivative, which shows that all six hydrogen atoms are equivalent.
(c) Benzene forms three isomeric disubstituted derivatives.
(d) Each carbon atom of benzene is sp³ hybridised.
(e) The six π electrons of benzene are localised in three separate π bonds.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: Kekulé's structure; one monosubstituted and three (o, m, p) disubstituted derivatives; each carbon sp² hybridised, with the six π electrons delocalised over the ring (the source of its stability).
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (d) or (e), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', structure of benzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hydration of an alkyne (with Hg²⁺ and dilute H₂SO₄) proceeds through an unstable enol, which changes into a carbonyl compound.
Statement II: Ethyne gives ethanal on hydration.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Water adds across the triple bond to give an enol (C=C–OH), which tautomerises to the more stable carbonyl compound. For ethyne this gives ethanal; higher alkynes give ketones.
steps: Statement II: HC≡CH + H₂O → [CH₂=CHOH] → CH₃CHO → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', chemical properties of alkynes (addition of water)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the chlorination of methane, light or heat brings about homolysis of the Cl–Cl bond in the initiation step.
Reason (R): The C–H bond is weaker than the Cl–Cl bond.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The chain is initiated by homolysis of Cl₂ because the Cl–Cl bond is weaker than the C–C and C–H bonds, so it breaks most easily. R states the opposite.
steps: R: Cl–Cl (≈242 kJ mol⁻¹) is weaker than C–H (≈435 kJ mol⁻¹) → R false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', halogenation of alkanes (mechanism)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 2.7 g of buta-1,3-diene, CH₂=CH–CH=CH₂, undergoes complete ozonolysis (O₃, then Zn/H₂O). The mass of methanal formed is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.explanation: Both double bonds are cleaved. The two terminal CH₂= groups become two HCHO, and the middle =CH–CH= unit becomes ethanedial, OHC–CHO.
steps: Each mole gives 2 mol HCHO + 1 mol OHC–CHO
solution.why_others_wrong: 2.9 g is the mass of ethanedial (0.050 × 58). 1.5 g counts only one HCHO per diene. 6.0 g counts four HCHO per diene.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', ozonolysis of alkenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following decolourise bromine water at room temperature?
Ethene, ethyne, benzene, cyclohexane, propene, cyclohexene, ethane

solution.concept: Addition of bromine as a test for unsaturation
solution.explanation: Compounds with C=C or C≡C bonds add bromine readily, so the reddish-brown colour disappears. Benzene, despite its formal unsaturation, does not add bromine under these conditions because of its aromatic stability; alkanes and cycloalkanes do not react.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 misses ethyne or cyclohexene. 5 or 6 count benzene and/or a saturated hydrocarbon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', addition of halogens (test for unsaturation); aromaticity

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the alkene in List-I with the products of its ozonolysis (O₃, then Zn/H₂O) in List-II.

List-I:
A. Propene
B. 2-Methylpropene
C. Pent-2-ene
D. But-1-ene

List-II:
I. Methanal and propanal
II. Ethanal and propanal
III. Methanal and propanone
IV. Methanal and ethanal

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Each carbon of the C=C becomes a C=O. CH₃CH=CH₂ → CH₃CHO + HCHO; (CH₃)₂C=CH₂ → (CH₃)₂CO + HCHO; CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₃ → CH₃CHO + CH₃CH₂CHO; CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂ → CH₃CH₂CHO + HCHO.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', ozonolysis of alkenes
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about benzene and arenes are correct?

(a) Polynuclear hydrocarbons with more than two fused benzene rings are toxic and are said to be carcinogenic.
(b) In the presence of ultraviolet light, benzene adds three molecules of chlorine to give benzene hexachloride, C₆H₆Cl₆.
(c) Arenes burn with a sooty flame.
(d) Friedel–Crafts methylation of benzene with CH₃Cl stops cleanly at toluene, because the methyl group deactivates the ring.
(e) Benzene is hydrogenated to cyclohexane at room temperature without a catalyst.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Statements (a)–(c) are NCERT facts. The methyl group activates the ring, so toluene reacts further and Friedel–Crafts alkylation tends to give polysubstitution. Hydrogenation of benzene needs a nickel catalyst and high temperature or pressure.
steps: (e) needs Ni, heat and pressure → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (d) or (e), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', aromatic hydrocarbons (properties; carcinogenicity and toxicity)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The correct order of reactivity towards nitration (electrophilic substitution) is:

solution.explanation: –CH₃ activates the ring (+I and hyperconjugation), so toluene reacts faster than benzene. –Cl deactivates slightly (−I outweighs +R) and –NO₂ deactivates strongly (−I and −R).
solution.why_others_wrong: Placing benzene above toluene ignores the activating methyl group. Placing chlorobenzene above benzene treats –Cl as activating, although its −I effect outweighs its +R effect.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', directive influence of a functional group in monosubstituted benzene
solution.final_answer: Option A: Toluene > benzene > chlorobenzene > nitrobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: When an alcohol is converted into an alkyl chloride with phosphorus pentachloride, the by-products are:

solution.explanation: R–OH + PCl₅ → R–Cl + POCl₃ + HCl.
steps: By-products: phosphorus oxychloride and hydrogen chloride
solution.why_others_wrong: SO₂ and HCl are the by-products with thionyl chloride. H₃PO₃ is the by-product with PCl₃ (3R–OH + PCl₃ → 3R–Cl + H₃PO₃). PCl₃ and Cl₂ are not formed.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', preparation of haloalkanes from alcohols

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A haloalkane, R–X, is treated with potassium nitrite, KNO₂. The main product is:

solution.concept: Nucleophilic substitution with the ambident nitrite ion
solution.explanation: The nitrite ion is ambident. With ionic KNO₂, attack occurs mainly through oxygen, giving the alkyl nitrite R–O–N=O. With covalent AgNO₂, attack occurs through nitrogen, giving the nitroalkane.
steps: KNO₂ → free NO₂⁻ attacks through O → R–O–N=O
solution.why_others_wrong: R–NO₂ is the main product with AgNO₂. Isocyanides come from AgCN, and alcohols from aqueous KOH.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nucleophilic substitution reactions (table of nucleophiles)
solution.final_answer: Option B: an alkyl nitrite, R–O–N=O

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 10.9 g of bromoethane is heated with sodium iodide in dry acetone and converted completely into iodoethane (Finkelstein reaction). The mass of iodoethane formed is (C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80, I = 127):

solution.explanation: C₂H₅Br + NaI → C₂H₅I + NaBr: 1 : 1 mole ratio.
solution.why_others_wrong: 14.2 g is the mass of 0.10 mol of iodomethane. 10.9 g assumes the mass does not change. 7.8 g halves the moles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', halogen exchange (Finkelstein reaction)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The order of reactivity of alcohols with a given halogen acid is 1° > 2° > 3°.
Statement II: The order of reactivity of the halogen acids with a given alcohol is HI > HBr > HCl.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Preparation of haloalkanes from alcohols and HX
solution.explanation: NCERT: the order of reactivity of alcohols with a given haloacid is 3° > 2° > 1°; tertiary alcohols react with concentrated HCl even at room temperature, while primary and secondary alcohols need ZnCl₂. For the acids, HI > HBr > HCl.
steps: Statement II: HI > HBr > HCl → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', preparation from alcohols
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 2-Bromopentane, heated with alcoholic KOH, gives pent-2-ene as the major product rather than pent-1-ene.
Reason (R): In dehydrohalogenation, the preferred alkene is the one with the greater number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms (Zaitsev rule).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: β-Hydrogen can be lost from C-1 (giving pent-1-ene, one alkyl group on the C=C) or from C-3 (giving pent-2-ene, two alkyl groups on the C=C). The more substituted alkene is preferred, as the rule states.
steps: R is the rule that predicts A → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', elimination reactions
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the common name in List-I with the formula in List-II.

List-I:
A. Ethylidene chloride
B. Ethylene dichloride
C. Methylene chloride
D. Vinyl chloride

List-II:
I. CH₂Cl₂
II. CH₂=CHCl
III. ClCH₂–CH₂Cl
IV. CH₃CHCl₂

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Common names of di- and polyhalogen compounds
solution.explanation: Ethylidene (CH₃CH=) gives the geminal dihalide CH₃CHCl₂ (1,1-dichloroethane). Ethylene dichloride is the vicinal dihalide ClCH₂CH₂Cl (1,2-dichloroethane). Methylene chloride is CH₂Cl₂ (dichloromethane). Vinyl chloride is CH₂=CHCl (chloroethene).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nomenclature (common names)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the physical properties of haloalkanes are correct?

(a) Methyl chloride, methyl bromide, ethyl chloride and some chlorofluoromethanes are gases at room temperature.
(b) All chloroalkanes are denser than water.
(c) For the same alkyl group, alkyl iodides have lower boiling points than alkyl chlorides.
(d) Haloalkanes tend to dissolve in organic solvents.
(e) Pure alkyl halides are colourless, but bromides and iodides develop colour on exposure to light.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the lower members listed are gases; bromo, iodo and polychloro derivatives are heavier than water, but monochloroalkanes such as n-propyl chloride are lighter; boiling points rise in the order RCl < RBr < RI with the increase in size and van der Waals forces; haloalkanes dissolve in organic solvents; bromides and iodides develop colour in light.
steps: (b) e.g. n-propyl chloride is lighter than water → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (b) or (c), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', physical properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 7.85 g of 2-chloropropane is heated with alcoholic KOH and the alkene formed is passed into bromine dissolved in CCl₄. Assuming both reactions are complete, the mass of the dibromo compound formed is (C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5, Br = 80):

solution.concept: Two-step stoichiometry: dehydrohalogenation, then addition of bromine
solution.explanation: CH₃CHClCH₃ → CH₃CH=CH₂ (alc. KOH); CH₃CH=CH₂ + Br₂ → CH₃CHBrCH₂Br (1,2-dibromopropane). Each step is 1 : 1.
solution.why_others_wrong: 18.8 g is the mass of 0.10 mol of 1,2-dibromoethane (the wrong alkene). 12.3 g is 0.10 mol of a monobromopropane (HBr instead of Br₂). 10.1 g halves the moles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', elimination reactions; Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', addition of halogens

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about haloarenes are correct?

(a) A nitro group meta to the chlorine has practically no effect on the reactivity of chlorobenzene towards nucleophiles.
(b) The C–Cl bond in chlorobenzene is shorter than in chloromethane, because the carbon bonded to Cl is sp² hybridised.
(c) Haloarenes are more reactive than haloalkanes towards nucleophilic substitution, because the sp² carbon is more electrophilic.
(d) Chlorobenzene is converted into phenol by aqueous NaOH at room temperature.
(e) 1-Chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene is hydrolysed under milder conditions than 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: An –NO₂ group at the ortho or para position stabilises the negative charge of the intermediate by resonance; at the meta position it cannot, so no effect is observed. More nitro groups at o/p allow milder conditions (4-nitro: 443 K; 2,4-dinitro: 368 K). The sp² carbon holds the C–Cl electron pair more tightly, giving a shorter, stronger bond; haloarenes are therefore less reactive, and chlorobenzene needs 623 K and 300 atm to give phenol.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (c) or (d), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', reactions of haloarenes (nucleophilic substitution)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Haloalkanes are only very slightly soluble in water.
Reason (R): The carbon–halogen bond in a haloalkane is non-polar.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The C–X bond is polar (halogen more electronegative than carbon). Haloalkanes are only slightly soluble because the energy released in forming new haloalkane–water attractions is less than the energy needed to break the hydrogen bonds between water molecules.
steps: A: only very slightly soluble → true
R: C–X is polar (C δ⁺, X δ⁻) → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nature of C–X bond; physical properties (solubility)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Benzal chloride, C₆H₅CHCl₂, obtained by side-chain chlorination of toluene, is hydrolysed at 373 K to benzaldehyde. The mass of benzaldehyde formed from 16.1 g of benzal chloride, assuming complete conversion, is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, Cl = 35.5):

solution.concept: Preparation of benzaldehyde from toluene via benzal chloride
solution.explanation: C₆H₅CHCl₂ + H₂O → C₆H₅CHO + 2HCl (the gem-diol formed loses water). Mole ratio 1 : 1.
solution.why_others_wrong: 12.2 g is 0.10 mol of benzoic acid (over-oxidation is not involved). 10.8 g is 0.10 mol of benzyl alcohol. 5.3 g halves the moles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', preparation of aromatic aldehydes (side-chain chlorination followed by hydrolysis)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 6.0 g of ethanoic acid is reduced completely with lithium aluminium hydride, and the product is hydrolysed. The mass of the organic product is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.explanation: LiAlH₄ reduces a carboxylic acid all the way to the primary alcohol: CH₃COOH → CH₃CH₂OH.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.4 g assumes the reduction stops at ethanal. 3.2 g is 0.10 mol of methanol (a carbon lost). 2.30 g halves the moles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', reactions of carboxylic acids (reduction)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Ethanoic acid is heated with P₂O₅, which removes water: 2CH₃COOH → (CH₃CO)₂O + H₂O. The mass of ethanoic anhydride obtained from 12.0 g of ethanoic acid, assuming complete conversion, is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.explanation: Two molecules of acid lose one molecule of water to give one molecule of anhydride.
solution.why_others_wrong: 20.4 g takes a 1 : 1 ratio. 5.1 g divides by 2 twice. 8.4 g subtracts one water for each molecule of acid (0.20 mol) instead of for each pair.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', formation of anhydride

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Acid-catalysed hydration of propene gives propan-1-ol as the main product.
Statement II: Catalytic hydrogenation of an aldehyde gives a secondary alcohol.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Preparation of alcohols from alkenes and carbonyl compounds
solution.explanation: Acid-catalysed hydration follows Markovnikov's rule: H adds to C-1 and OH to C-2, giving propan-2-ol. Hydrogenation (H₂ with Pt, Pd or Ni) of an aldehyde gives a primary alcohol; ketones give secondary alcohols.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', preparation of alcohols
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Benzoic acid is highly soluble in cold water.
Reason (R): Aliphatic carboxylic acids with up to four carbon atoms are miscible with water because they form hydrogen bonds with it.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: simple aliphatic acids up to four carbons are miscible with water (hydrogen bonding); solubility falls as the hydrocarbon part grows, and benzoic acid is nearly insoluble in cold water.
steps: A: benzoic acid is nearly insoluble in cold water → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', physical properties of carboxylic acids
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the alcohol in List-I with its class in List-II.

List-I:
A. CH₂=CH–CH₂–OH
B. C₆H₅–CH₂–OH
C. CH₂=CH–OH
D. (CH₃)₃C–OH

List-II:
I. Vinylic alcohol
II. Benzylic alcohol
III. Tertiary (3°) alcohol
IV. Allylic alcohol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In an allylic alcohol the –OH is on an sp³ carbon next to a C=C; in a benzylic alcohol it is on an sp³ carbon next to a benzene ring; in a vinylic alcohol it is on a C=C carbon itself; a tertiary alcohol has the –OH on a carbon bonded to three other carbons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', classification
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 4.1 g of ethanenitrile, CH₃CN, is treated with an excess of phenylmagnesium bromide, and the product is hydrolysed. Assuming complete conversion, the mass of ketone formed is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16):

solution.concept: Preparation of ketones from nitriles and Grignard reagents
solution.explanation: The Grignard reagent adds to the C≡N group; hydrolysis of the imine salt gives a ketone: CH₃CN + C₆H₅MgBr → (H₃O⁺) C₆H₅COCH₃ (acetophenone).
solution.why_others_wrong: 12.2 g is 0.10 mol of benzoic acid and 10.6 g is 0.10 mol of benzaldehyde; neither is formed. 6.0 g halves the moles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', preparation of ketones from nitriles

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 15.8 g of benzenesulphonic acid is fused with molten NaOH, and the product is acidified. Assuming complete conversion, the mass of phenol formed is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, S = 32, Na = 23):

solution.concept: Preparation of phenol from benzenesulphonic acid
solution.explanation: C₆H₅SO₃H → (fused NaOH) C₆H₅ONa → (H⁺) C₆H₅OH. One mole of sulphonic acid gives one mole of phenol.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11.6 g is the mass of sodium phenoxide, before acidification. 7.8 g is 0.10 mol of benzene. 4.7 g halves the moles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', preparation of phenols (from benzenesulphonic acid)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 10.8 g of anisole (methoxybenzene) is heated with excess HI until it is completely cleaved. The mass of the alkyl iodide formed is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, I = 127):

solution.concept: Cleavage of alkyl aryl ethers by HI
solution.explanation: The O–CH₃ bond breaks (the O–aryl bond has partial double bond character), so the products are phenol and methyl iodide: C₆H₅OCH₃ + HI → C₆H₅OH + CH₃I.
solution.why_others_wrong: 20.4 g is 0.10 mol of iodobenzene, which is not formed. 9.4 g is the mass of phenol, the other product. 7.1 g halves the moles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', reactions of ethers (cleavage of C–O bond)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Nitration of benzaldehyde gives mainly o- and p-nitrobenzaldehyde.
Statement II: Bromination of benzoic acid in the presence of FeBr₃ gives mainly p-bromobenzoic acid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both –CHO and –COOH are electron-withdrawing, deactivating and meta-directing. Nitration of benzaldehyde gives m-nitrobenzaldehyde, and bromination of benzoic acid gives m-bromobenzoic acid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', electrophilic substitution reactions
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The addition of HCN to ethanal is catalysed by a base.
Reason (R): The base converts HCN into the cyanide ion, a stronger nucleophile, which adds readily to the carbonyl carbon.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: With pure HCN the reaction is very slow. A base generates CN⁻, which is a much stronger nucleophile than HCN; it attacks the carbonyl carbon, and the alkoxide formed takes a proton from HCN to give the cyanohydrin.
steps: A: base catalyses the reaction → true
R: base gives CN⁻, the stronger nucleophile → true
That is why the base speeds up the addition → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', nucleophilic addition (addition of HCN)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Each reagent in List-I reacts with a carbonyl compound, >C=O. Match it with the group formed in the product (List-II).

List-I:
A. Hydrazine, NH₂NH₂
B. Phenylhydrazine, C₆H₅NHNH₂
C. Semicarbazide, NH₂CONHNH₂
D. Hydroxylamine, NH₂OH

List-II:
I. >C=N–OH
II. >C=N–NH–CO–NH₂
III. >C=N–NH₂
IV. >C=N–NH–C₆H₅

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Ammonia derivatives Z–NH₂ condense with the carbonyl group, losing water, to give >C=N–Z: hydrazone (Z = NH₂), phenylhydrazone (Z = NHC₆H₅), semicarbazone (Z = NHCONH₂) and oxime (Z = OH).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', reactions with ammonia and its derivatives
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about carboxylic acids and their derivatives are correct?

(a) Carboxylic acids react with PCl₃ to give acyl chlorides.
(b) Nitriles are hydrolysed, through amides, to carboxylic acids in the presence of H⁺ or OH⁻.
(c) Carboxylic acids react with alkalis but not with metals such as sodium.
(d) Esterification of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol is an irreversible reaction.
(e) Acyl chlorides and acid anhydrides are hydrolysed by water to give carboxylic acids.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Preparation and reactions of carboxylic acids
solution.explanation: NCERT: acids give acyl chlorides with PCl₅, PCl₃ or SOCl₂; nitriles are hydrolysed to amides and then to acids; acids react with electropositive metals (liberating H₂) as well as with alkalis; esterification is reversible, so water is removed to shift the equilibrium; acyl chlorides and anhydrides are hydrolysed to acids.
steps: (c) they react with Na too (H₂ evolved) → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (c) or (d), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', methods of preparation and chemical reactions of carboxylic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following can undergo self aldol condensation in the presence of dilute alkali?
Ethanal, propanone, methanal, benzaldehyde, 2,2-dimethylpropanal, acetophenone, propanal

solution.concept: Requirement of an α-hydrogen for aldol condensation
solution.explanation: Aldol condensation needs at least one α-hydrogen, which the base removes to form the carbanion (enolate). Methanal and benzaldehyde have no α-carbon bearing hydrogen; in 2,2-dimethylpropanal, (CH₃)₃C–CHO, the α-carbon carries no hydrogen.
steps: α-H present: ethanal, propanone, acetophenone (CH₃ group), propanal
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 usually misses acetophenone, whose methyl group supplies α-hydrogens. 5 counts 2,2-dimethylpropanal, whose α-carbon is quaternary. 7 counts every carbonyl compound.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', aldol condensation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following are stronger acids than phenol?
Ethanol, p-nitrophenol, o-cresol, picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol), water, m-nitrophenol, p-cresol

solution.concept: Effect of substituents on the acidity of phenol
solution.explanation: Electron-withdrawing –NO₂ groups stabilise the phenoxide ion and increase acidity (pKa: p-nitrophenol 7.1, m-nitrophenol 8.3, picric acid 0.71, against phenol 10.0). Electron-releasing –CH₃ groups decrease it (cresols pKa about 10.2). Ethanol (15.9) and water are weaker acids than phenol.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 leaves out m-nitrophenol (–NO₂ still withdraws electrons by −I at the meta position). 4 or 5 count a cresol, whose methyl group makes it a weaker acid than phenol.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', acidity of phenols (pKa table)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Compound X, C₅H₁₀O, does not reduce Tollens' reagent but gives a yellow precipitate with iodine and NaOH. On Clemmensen reduction, X gives n-pentane. X is:

solution.concept: Identifying a carbonyl compound from its tests
solution.explanation: No Tollens' test → a ketone, not an aldehyde. Iodoform test → a CH₃CO– group. Clemmensen reduction gives the alkane with the same carbon skeleton, so the chain must be unbranched.
solution.why_others_wrong: Pentan-3-one has no CH₃CO– group, so it gives no iodoform. 3-Methylbutan-2-one gives 2-methylbutane, not n-pentane. Pentanal is an aldehyde and reduces Tollens' reagent.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', chemical reactions (Clemmensen reduction, haloform reaction, Tollens' test)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about ethers are correct?

(a) Anisole reacts with CH₃Cl and anhydrous AlCl₃ to give mainly 2- and 4-methoxytoluene.
(b) Nitration of anisole gives mainly 2- and 4-nitroanisole.
(c) In the cleavage of ethers, the order of reactivity of the hydrogen halides is HI > HBr > HCl.
(d) Ethers are prepared in good yield by heating tertiary alcohols with concentrated H₂SO₄ at 413 K.
(e) Molecules of methoxymethane form hydrogen bonds with one another, like those of ethanol.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The –OCH₃ group activates the ring and directs to ortho and para positions (Friedel–Crafts, nitration). NCERT gives the order HI > HBr > HCl for cleavage. Acid dehydration of tertiary alcohols gives alkenes, because elimination competes. Ethers have no O–H, so they cannot hydrogen bond with one another.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (d) or (e), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', ethers (preparation, physical and chemical properties)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the acid-catalysed dehydration of ethanol to ethene, the first step is protonation of the oxygen atom of the alcohol.
Statement II: The last step of this mechanism is the loss of a water molecule from the carbocation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Mechanism of acid-catalysed dehydration of alcohols
solution.explanation: Step 1: protonation of the alcohol to give the oxonium ion. Step 2: loss of water to give the carbocation (the slowest, rate-determining step). Step 3: loss of a proton from the carbocation to give the alkene.
steps: Statement I: protonation is step 1 → true
Statement II: water is lost in step 2; step 3 is loss of H⁺ → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', dehydration of alcohols (mechanism)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Phenol is a weaker acid than ethanoic acid.
Reason (R): In the ethanoate ion the negative charge is delocalised over two electronegative oxygen atoms, whereas in the phenoxide ion it is delocalised over the less electronegative carbon atoms of the ring.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Relative acidity of carboxylic acids and phenols
solution.explanation: The carboxylate ion has two equivalent resonance structures with the negative charge on oxygen, so it is much more stabilised than phenoxide, where the canonical structures place the charge on ring carbons. The more stable conjugate base means the stronger acid.
steps: Stability of the conjugate base decides acidity → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', acidity of carboxylic acids
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The amine (CH₃)₃C–NH₂ (2-methylpropan-2-amine) is classified as a:

solution.explanation: Amines are classified by the number of hydrogen atoms of NH₃ replaced by alkyl or aryl groups, not by the nature of the carbon bearing the nitrogen. Here only one H is replaced (by a tert-butyl group), so it is a primary amine.
steps: N bonded to one carbon group and two H atoms
(The carbon attached to N is tertiary, but that does not decide the class of an amine)
solution.why_others_wrong: Secondary and tertiary amines have two and three carbon groups on nitrogen. A quaternary ammonium compound has four groups on a positively charged nitrogen.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', structure and classification of amines

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 9.3 g of aniline is diazotised. The diazonium salt is converted into its fluoroborate, which is treated with aqueous sodium nitrite in the presence of copper powder, so that the diazo group is replaced by –NO₂. Assuming every step is complete, the mass of nitrobenzene formed is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16):

solution.concept: Replacement of the diazo group by a nitro group
solution.explanation: C₆H₅NH₂ → C₆H₅N₂⁺ → C₆H₅N₂⁺BF₄⁻ → (NaNO₂, Cu) C₆H₅NO₂ + N₂. Every step is 1 : 1.
solution.why_others_wrong: 10.3 g is 0.10 mol of benzonitrile (the CuCN product). 15.7 g is 0.10 mol of bromobenzene. 6.2 g halves the moles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', reactions of diazonium salts (replacement by nitro group)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Amines behave as Lewis bases because:

options.text: they contain hydrogen atoms bonded to nitrogen
nitrogen is more electronegative than carbon
the nitrogen atom has an unshared pair of electrons

solution.explanation: The lone pair on nitrogen can be donated to an electron-pair acceptor such as H⁺ (forming R–NH₃⁺) or a Lewis acid. That is what makes amines bases.
steps: Nitrogen in amines: three bonds + one lone pair
Lone pair donated to H⁺ → ammonium ion
solution.why_others_wrong: Tertiary amines have no N–H bond yet are bases. The electronegativity of N and water solubility do not by themselves make a compound a base (higher amines are insoluble but still basic).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', chemical reactions (basic character of amines)
solution.final_answer: Option D: the nitrogen atom has an unshared pair of electrons

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Primary amines have lower boiling points than alcohols of comparable molecular mass.
Statement II: Methanamine reacts with benzoyl chloride to give N-methylbenzamide.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The N–H···N hydrogen bond is weaker than O–H···O because nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen, so amines boil lower than comparable alcohols (e.g. n-butylamine 350.8 K vs butan-1-ol 390.3 K). NCERT gives benzoylation: CH₃NH₂ + C₆H₅COCl → C₆H₅CONHCH₃ + HCl.
steps: Statement I: weaker H-bonding in amines → true
Statement II: benzoylation gives N-methylbenzamide → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', physical properties; chemical reactions (benzoylation)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An aqueous solution of methylamine gives a precipitate of ferric hydroxide with FeCl₃ solution.
Reason (R): Methylamine is a base; in water it accepts a proton and produces hydroxide ions.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Basicity of aliphatic amines in water
solution.explanation: CH₃NH₂ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃NH₃⁺ + OH⁻. The hydroxide ions precipitate Fe³⁺ as hydrated ferric oxide: Fe³⁺ + 3OH⁻ → Fe(OH)₃.
steps: A: brown precipitate of Fe(OH)₃ → true
R: CH₃NH₂ produces OH⁻ in water → true
The OH⁻ produced is what precipitates Fe(OH)₃ → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', basic character of amines
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the amine in List-I with its IUPAC name in List-II.

List-I:
A. C₆H₅N(CH₃)₂
B. CH₃CH₂NHCH₃
C. (C₂H₅)₃N
D. H₂N–CH₂–CH₂–NH₂

List-II:
I. Ethane-1,2-diamine
II. N,N-Diethylethanamine
III. N-Methylethanamine
IV. N,N-Dimethylbenzenamine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The longest alkyl chain (or benzene) gives the parent amine; other groups on nitrogen are cited with the locant N. A diamine gets the suffix -diamine with the locants of both nitrogen-bearing carbons.
steps: A: benzenamine with two N-methyls → N,N-dimethylbenzenamine (IV)
B: ethanamine with one N-methyl → N-methylethanamine (III)
C: ethanamine with two N-ethyls → N,N-diethylethanamine (II)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the basic strength of amines are correct?

(a) In aqueous solution, the basic strength of an amine is decided by the combination of the inductive effect, solvation and steric hindrance of the alkyl groups.
(b) The larger the Kb of an amine, the weaker it is as a base.
(c) The smaller the pKb of an amine, the stronger it is as a base.
(d) Bulky alkyl groups on nitrogen hinder the hydrogen bonding (solvation) of the substituted ammonium ion with water, which lowers the basic strength.
(e) Among the ethyl-substituted amines in water, triethylamine is the strongest base.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Basicity of amines: Kb, pKb and the factors involved
solution.explanation: A larger Kb (smaller pKb) means a stronger base. In water, +I effect, solvation of the ammonium ion and steric hindrance together decide basicity; for the ethyl series the order is (C₂H₅)₂NH > (C₂H₅)₃N > C₂H₅NH₂ > NH₃.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (b) or (e), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', basic character of amines (structure–basicity relationship)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
In the Hofmann bromamide degradation,
RCONH₂ + Br₂ + 4NaOH → RNH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2NaBr + 2H₂O
the minimum mass of NaOH needed to convert 5.9 g of ethanamide completely into methanamine is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16, Na = 23):

solution.concept: Stoichiometry of the Hofmann bromamide reaction
solution.explanation: Four moles of NaOH are used per mole of amide (to form NaBr, Na₂CO₃ and to neutralise the reaction intermediates).
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.0 g, 8.0 g and 12.0 g take 1, 2 or 3 mol of NaOH per mole of amide instead of the 4 shown in the balanced equation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', preparation of amines (Hofmann bromamide degradation)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 9.3 g of aniline is acetylated with ethanoic anhydride; the product is brominated with Br₂ in ethanoic acid to give the para-bromo compound, which is then hydrolysed. Assuming every step is complete, the mass of the final product is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16, Br = 80):

solution.concept: Controlling the reactivity of aniline by acetylation
solution.explanation: Acetylation moderates the activating –NH₂ group so that only monobromination occurs (at the para position). Hydrolysis then removes the acetyl group, giving 4-bromoaniline.
solution.why_others_wrong: 13.5 g is the mass of acetanilide and 21.4 g that of p-bromoacetanilide (the steps before hydrolysis). 33.0 g is 2,4,6-tribromoaniline, formed only if aniline itself is brominated.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', electrophilic substitution (bromination of aniline via acetanilide)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ethanol reduces benzenediazonium chloride to benzene.
Reason (R): In this reaction, ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Replacement of the diazo group by hydrogen
solution.explanation: Mild reducing agents such as hypophosphorous acid or ethanol replace –N₂⁺ by –H. NCERT's equation: ArN₂⁺Cl⁻ + CH₃CH₂OH → ArH + N₂ + CH₃CHO + HCl. Ethanol is oxidised only to ethanal.
steps: R: the oxidation product is ethanal, not ethanoic acid → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', reactions of diazonium salts (replacement by hydrogen)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Commercially, glucose is obtained by boiling which substance with dilute H₂SO₄ at 393 K under 2–3 bar pressure?

solution.explanation: NCERT: glucose is obtained commercially by hydrolysis of starch: (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ + nH₂O → nC₆H₁₂O₆ (dilute H₂SO₄, 393 K, 2–3 bar). In the laboratory it is made by boiling sucrose with dilute acid, which gives glucose and fructose.
solution.why_others_wrong: Sucrose hydrolysis is the laboratory method and also gives fructose. Lactose gives galactose as well. Cellulose is not the commercial source NCERT describes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', preparation of glucose

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the vitamin in List-I with a source of it in List-II.

List-I:
A. Vitamin D
B. Vitamin E

D. Vitamin B₁₂

List-II:
I. Citrus fruits, amla and green leafy vegetables
II. Exposure to sunlight; fish and egg yolk
III. Meat, fish, egg and curd
IV. Vegetable oils such as wheat germ oil and sunflower oil

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: From NCERT's table: vitamin D – exposure to sunlight, fish and egg yolk; vitamin E – vegetable oils like wheat germ oil and sunflower oil; vitamin C – citrus fruits, amla and green leafy vegetables; vitamin B₁₂ – meat, fish, egg and curd.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', vitamins (sources and deficiency diseases table)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Amylose is insoluble in water, whereas amylopectin is water soluble.
Statement II: Cellulose is a branched-chain polymer of β-D-glucose units.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: amylose is the water-soluble component of starch (15–20%) and amylopectin is insoluble in water. Cellulose is a straight-chain polysaccharide of β-D-glucose units joined by C1–C4 glycosidic linkages.
steps: Statement II: cellulose is unbranched → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', polysaccharides
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 20% of the bases are adenine. The percentage of cytosine is:

solution.explanation: In double-stranded DNA, adenine pairs with thymine and guanine with cytosine, so A = T and G = C.
solution.why_others_wrong: 20% equates cytosine with adenine. 60% is G + C together. 40% is A + T.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', structure of nucleic acids (base pairing)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In a nucleoside, the base is attached to the pentose sugar at its:

solution.explanation: NCERT: a unit formed by the attachment of a base to the 1′ position of the sugar is a nucleoside. When the 5′ position of the sugar carries a phosphate, the unit is a nucleotide.
solution.why_others_wrong: The 5′ position carries the phosphate in a nucleotide, and 3′ and 5′ are joined in the phosphodiester links of the chain. The 2′ position differs between ribose (OH) and deoxyribose (H).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', chemical composition and structure of nucleic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Almost all enzymes are globular proteins.
Reason (R): Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and for a particular substrate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements are NCERT facts about enzymes. That enzymes are proteins with a globular shape does not follow from their specificity, and their specificity is not why they are proteins, so R does not explain A.
steps: A: enzymes are biocatalysts, almost all globular proteins → true
R describes a different property → not the explanation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about nucleic acids are correct?

(a) The double-helix structure of DNA was proposed by James Watson and Francis Crick.
(b) In nucleic acids, nucleotides are joined by phosphodiester linkages between the 5′ and 3′ carbon atoms of the pentose sugars.
(c) DNA contains uracil.
(d) Adenine and guanine are pyrimidine bases.
(e) The sugar in RNA lacks an –OH group at the 2′ position.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Watson and Crick proposed the double helix; nucleotides are linked by 5′–3′ phosphodiester bonds. DNA contains A, G, C and T (uracil occurs in RNA instead of thymine). Adenine and guanine are purines; cytosine, thymine and uracil are pyrimidines. Ribose in RNA has a 2′-OH; deoxyribose in DNA lacks it.
steps: (d) A and G are purines → false
(e) it is deoxyribose (DNA) that lacks the 2′-OH → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (c), (d) or (e), all false, or leaves out (a) or (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', nucleic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 8.1 g of a polysaccharide (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ is hydrolysed completely to glucose, and all the glucose is fermented: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. The volume of CO₂ at STP is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16; molar volume at STP = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.concept: Hydrolysis of a polysaccharide and fermentation of glucose
solution.explanation: Each C₆H₁₀O₅ unit (162 g mol⁻¹) gives one glucose molecule on hydrolysis, and each glucose gives two CO₂.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.12 L takes one CO₂ per glucose. 4.48 L doubles again. 2.02 L uses 180 g mol⁻¹ (glucose) instead of 162 g mol⁻¹ for the polysaccharide unit.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', polysaccharides; Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', ethanol by fermentation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A protein found in a biological system with a unique three-dimensional structure and biological activity is called a native protein.
Statement II: The main forces that stabilise the secondary and tertiary structures of proteins are hydrogen bonds, disulphide linkages, van der Waals forces and electrostatic forces of attraction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Native proteins and the forces that stabilise protein structure
solution.explanation: Both are NCERT statements. When these stabilising interactions are disturbed (by heat or change of pH), the protein loses its biological activity: denaturation.
steps: Statement I: definition of native protein → true
Statement II: true as NCERT lists them
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', structure of proteins; denaturation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

Match the amino acid in List-I with its one-letter code in List-II.

List-I:
A. Lysine
B. Phenylalanine
C. Tyrosine
D. Tryptophan

List-II:
I. Y
II. W
III. K
IV. F

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT's table of amino acids gives: lysine K, phenylalanine F, tyrosine Y, tryptophan W (the first letters L, P and T belong to leucine, proline and threonine).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', amino acids (table of natural amino acids)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A ferric hydroxide sol is prepared by adding ferric chloride solution drop by drop to:

solution.concept: Preparation of a lyophobic sol by hydrolysis
solution.explanation: FeCl₃ is hydrolysed in boiling water: FeCl₃ + 3H₂O → Fe(OH)₃ (sol) + 3HCl, giving a reddish-brown sol. The Fe(OH)₃ particles adsorb Fe³⁺ ions, which keep the sol stable.
steps: Add FeCl₃ dropwise to boiling water
solution.why_others_wrong: In cold water hydrolysis is too slow. NaOH or NH₄OH solution gives a precipitate of Fe(OH)₃, not a sol.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), preparation of lyophobic sols (ferric hydroxide)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The volume of 0.10 M oxalic acid solution needed to prepare 250 mL of 0.020 M oxalic acid solution by dilution is:

solution.explanation: The number of moles of solute does not change on dilution.
steps: V₁ = 50 mL (made up to 250 mL with water)
solution.why_others_wrong: 200 mL is the water added, not the volume of stock solution. 1250 mL inverts the ratio of molarities. 5.0 mL uses 1.0 M for the stock solution.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), titrimetric analysis (preparation of standard solutions)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Starch forms a lyophilic sol when warmed and stirred with water.
Statement II: Arsenious sulphide forms a lyophilic sol.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Starch, gum and egg albumin form lyophilic (solvent-loving) sols directly with water. Arsenious sulphide sol is lyophobic; it is prepared by a chemical reaction (double decomposition of As₂O₃ with H₂S).
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), preparation of lyophilic and lyophobic sols
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 13.5 g of acetanilide is nitrated to p-nitroacetanilide, and the yield of the purified product is 70%. The mass of p-nitroacetanilide obtained is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16):

solution.concept: Percentage yield in a laboratory preparation
solution.explanation: C₆H₅NHCOCH₃ + HNO₃ → p-O₂NC₆H₄NHCOCH₃ + H₂O; one mole of acetanilide gives at most one mole of product.
solution.why_others_wrong: 18.0 g is the theoretical (100%) yield. 9.45 g takes 70% of the mass of acetanilide. 9.66 g is 70% of 0.10 mol of p-nitroaniline, the product after hydrolysis, which is not formed here.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), preparation of p-nitroacetanilide

questions.subtopic: Detection of elements and functional groups
questions.question_text:
Match the substance or group in List-I with the observation in its laboratory test in List-II.

List-I:
A. Carbohydrate (Molisch's test)
B. Oil or fat (heating with KHSO₄)
C. Protein (ninhydrin test)
D. Ketone (sodium nitroprusside test)

List-II:
I. Violet ring at the junction of the two layers
II. Blue-violet colour
III. Red colour in alkaline solution
IV. Pungent smell of acrolein

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Tests for carbohydrates, fats, proteins and ketones
solution.explanation: Molisch's test (α-naphthol, then conc. H₂SO₄ down the side) gives a violet ring for carbohydrates. Heating a fat or oil with KHSO₄ gives acrolein, with a pungent smell. Ninhydrin gives a blue-violet colour with proteins (amino acids). Ketones such as propanone give a red colour with sodium nitroprusside in alkali.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), tests for carbohydrates, fats and proteins; tests for functional groups
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A solution contains both oxalic acid and sodium oxalate. 25.0 mL of it needs 20.0 mL of 0.10 M NaOH for neutralisation (phenolphthalein). Another 25.0 mL portion, acidified with dilute H₂SO₄ and warmed, needs 40.0 mL of 0.020 M KMnO₄. The molarity of sodium oxalate in the solution is:

solution.concept: Combining an acid–base titration with a redox titration
solution.explanation: Only oxalic acid (dibasic) reacts with NaOH, but both oxalic acid and oxalate ions are oxidised by permanganate (2MnO₄⁻ : 5C₂O₄²⁻).
steps: Sodium oxalate = 2.0 − 1.0 = 1.0 mmol in 25.0 mL → 0.040 M
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.080 M is the total oxalate (oxalic acid not subtracted). 0.120 M adds the oxalic acid instead of subtracting it. 0.024 M takes the MnO₄⁻ : C₂O₄²⁻ ratio as 1 : 2.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), titrimetric analysis (oxalic acid against NaOH and against KMnO₄)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following observations in salt analysis are correctly described?

(a) Al³⁺: the white gelatinous precipitate of group III, dissolved in dilute HCl and treated with blue litmus and NH₄OH, gives a blue 'lake'.
(b) Mg²⁺ is precipitated in group V by ammonium carbonate in the presence of NH₄Cl and NH₄OH.
(c) Zn²⁺ is precipitated in group IV as a black sulphide.
(d) A nitrite gives brown fumes when warmed with dilute H₂SO₄.
(e) A phosphate gives a yellow precipitate when heated with concentrated HNO₃ and ammonium molybdate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Identification of cations and anions in salt analysis
solution.explanation: Al(OH)₃ adsorbs litmus to give a blue lake. Mg²⁺ is not precipitated in group V (the NH₄⁺ salts keep MgCO₃ in solution); it is detected in group VI with disodium hydrogen phosphate. ZnS is white (MnS buff, NiS and CoS black). Nitrite gives brown NO₂ with dilute acid (nitrate needs concentrated acid). Phosphate gives yellow ammonium phosphomolybdate.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (b) or (c), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), systematic qualitative analysis of cations and anions
